title: ETA Calculator: Arrival Time from Distance
description: Turn distance and speed into a duration and arrival time with the ETA Calculator — the simple, transparent trip estimate. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 340 miles at a 55 mph average is 6 hours 11 minutes — leave at 08:15 and the honest arrival is about 14:26, breaks not included.
quick_answer: The ETA Calculator converts a trip's distance and your expected average speed into a duration and an estimated arrival time. Set the origin and destination, or enter the distance directly, and read the simple estimate — transparent arithmetic you can adjust with stops and judgement, not a black box.

faq: No. This is distance ÷ your average speed — an estimate whose honesty comes from the average you choose. Live traffic is a navigation app's layer, not this calculation's.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Use the road distance from the Driving Distance Calculator or your ETA inherits the crow's optimism.
Can route results change over time?
Your average changes with season, load and route. The arithmetic is fixed; recalibrate the input per journey type.
Yes, on top of the rolling duration. The worked example adds lunch explicitly — make your stops explicit too.
What average speed should I use?
The one your similar completed journeys actually averaged — typically well below the speed limit once towns and stops bite. First time on a route, plan slower.
Yes — km ÷ km/h gives hours identically. The table includes a 100 km/h column for the metric habit.
ETA or duration — which does it give?
Both: the duration from distance and speed, and the arrival clock time when you give a departure.
